title: The First Inscription Site

features.name: founding stone
features.desc-on-touch: A grey-black rock, weathered, with a single line carved into it. The line could be an 'I' or a '|' or simply the mark of a tool on stone. The first mark. Everything after is commentary on this.

features.name: keeper's shelter
features.desc-on-touch: A small structure, ancient-looking, built around the stone. Not a museum—a living place. Someone has always been here, watching the mark, tending it.

features.name: inscription-echo
features.desc-on-touch: The ground here holds impressions of hands that have touched the stone over centuries. Each touch leaves a faint mark. The echoes of the first inscription continue.

features.name: archive-tower
features.desc-on-touch: A stack of stones, carefully placed, each one inscribed with the date it was added. A growing record of witnesses to the first mark. The tower will stand as long as someone comes to add a stone.

features.name: silence-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A depression in the earth that fills with rainwater. Perfectly still. In its surface you see the first mark reflected—not the stone's mark, but the moment before marking, the refusal to mark.

inscription: here silence learns the shape of its own refusal

reverie.title: REVERIE — first marking, light through leaves
narr: You kneel beside her at the stone. She holds the
tool—a stick charred at the end. 'Should we?' you
ask. She's quiet a long time. Then she touches the
stone without marking. 'The refusal,' she says, 'is
the mark.' So you both stay there, hands on silence,
and the stone keeps its first shape.

exits.label: back down to where silence still holds pristine
toward the threshold where the first word was almost spoken
to where witnesses gather to read the stone
into the forest where marking begins as growth
